summary.howTo: Each indicator has a chart comparing the class's repositories, with the class median marked on each bar. The comparison describes position, not a grade: what is good or bad depends on what the course asked for.
summary.solo: Every analyzed repository has a single author. Approval by someone else at 0% and concentration at 100% follow from that, not from a process problem.
summary.lowerBound: AI indicators are a lower bound: they only count what left a trace (declared co-authorship, agents, configuration files). No trace does not mean no AI.
summary.duplicates: Duplicates (same repository listed more than once): {{count}}

label.noData: No repository had this indicator measured.

reading.none: This indicator could not be measured in any of the {{count}} analyzed repositories.
reading.range: Across {{count}} measured repositories, values range from {{min}} to {{max}}, with a median of {{median}}.
reading.outlier: {{label}} ({{value}}) is well above the class median ({{median}}).
reading.solo: Single-author projects: this value reflects that.
reading.lowerBound: This is a lower bound: actual AI use may be higher.
reading.sampled_one: {{count}} repository was measured on a partial sample.
reading.sampled_other: {{count}} repositories were measured on a partial sample.

items.period: Analyzed period: {{from}} to {{to}}. Commits and merged PRs are those of the period; so are releases and CI runs.
items.privacy: The report uses repository-level data only. Nothing per student is included.
items.samples: Commits: up to {{commitCap}} of the period. PRs: searched among the {{prScan}} most recently updated merged PRs. "At least" and "partial sample" mark that cut.
items.nd: n/a means the data could not be measured (network failure, permission or missing source), never zero.
items.ai: No trace does not mean no AI. AI indicators and the badge measure observable practices, not actual use.

commit-activity.name: Commits in the period
commit-activity.what: Total commits in the repository within the class period, as GitHub counts them (merges and bots included).
commit-activity.read: Shows how much work was versioned in the period. Compare pace between teams carefully: scope differs from project to project.
commit-activity.limits: Commit volume does not measure effort or relevance. A large commit and a small one count the same.

contributors.name: Active authors
contributors.what: Number of people who committed in the class period, without bots and merge commits.
contributors.read: Helps see whether the whole team contributed. In an individual project the value is 1 by definition.
contributors.limits: Counts commit authors: the same person with different accounts or names may count twice, and someone who only reviewed or filed issues does not appear.

bus-factor.name: Concentration in the main author
bus-factor.what: Share of the author with the most commits among human commits (no bots or merges) in the period, without naming them.
bus-factor.read: High concentration means one person does almost everything and is worth a conversation with the team. In an individual project it will be 100%.
bus-factor.limits: Counts commits, not reviews or other contributions. On a very large history it uses the most recent sample of commits in the period.

prs-merges.name: Merged PRs
prs-merges.what: PRs merged within the class period, searched among the {{prScan}} most recently updated merged PRs.
prs-merges.limits: If the search limit is reached the value is a minimum (shown as "at least"). Volume says nothing about the quality of contributions.

lead-time.what: Median time between opening a PR and merging it, among PRs merged in the period, without bots. PRs opened by AI agents are left out and appear in "AI in the Process".
lead-time.limits: Only PRs merged in the period (closed without merge do not count), over a limited sample: "partial sample" marks the cut. Small maintenance PRs pull the median down.

review-coverage.what: Share of PRs merged in the period approved by someone other than the author before merging, without bots and without AI agent PRs.

first-review.what: Median time between a PR becoming ready for review and the first review by someone else before merging, over PRs merged in the period.

pr-size.what: Median changed lines (added + removed) per PR merged in the period.

ci-health.what: Success rate of GitHub Actions runs triggered by a push to the main branch within the period (up to 100 completed runs).
ci-health.limits: GitHub Actions only. Cancelled and skipped runs are not counted, so n can be smaller. n = 0 means no run in the period, not that CI failed.

conventional-commits.what: Share of the period's commits (up to {{commitCap}}, without merges and bots) whose first line follows type(scope)!: description.

release-cadence.what: Releases published on GitHub within the class period (dated by the tag, or by publication if the tag is later).
release-cadence.limits: Projects that only create tags, without GitHub releases, do not appear. Only the 100 most recent releases are read: if all fall in the period the value is a minimum. The ideal frequency depends on the kind of project.
